newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa seeks assurances before buying Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa seeks assurances before buying Iraqi oil.

text.p: South African oil buyers said on Tuesday they wanted safety and quality assurances from Iraq before considering buying the country's crude oil under the U.N. approved oil-for-food exchange.
They said they wanted confirmation of the quality of the oil being sold and the safety of ships using Iraq's Mina al-Bakr export terminal before they would consider Iraqi oil purchases.
South Africa has traditionally bought most of its crude from Iran and Kuwait.
One buyer said he had inquired about Iraqi oil but was not aware of any South African purchases yet.
"There are a whole lot of ifs, buts and maybes but subject to the price being right, and guarantees of quality, we could be buying from them," he said.
Buyers said they were likely to hang back until the first deliveries were made and quality assured.

They added that any purchases from Iraq would have to wait until next year because crude buying programmes had been completed fairly well in advance and January loading programmes had already been completed.
"So the next opportunity for South African refineries to secure oil would be early February. I very much doubt you will see any of the Iraqi crude heading this way this year," one buyer said.
